## The question

[Persistent random steps decorations during beamer \uncover](https://tex.stackexchange.com/questions/13580/persistent-random-steps-decorations-during-beamer-uncover), asked by [Derek](https://tex.stackexchange.com/users/4199/derek) on TeX Stack Exchange (2011-03-16; [CC BY-SA 2.5](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/2.5/)):

> I'm using a random steps decoration with a path that appears through several uncover transitions.  Currently the decoration is redrawn in each instance of the slide.  How can I change this behavior.  A minimal example follows.  Thanks.
>
> ```latex
> \documentclass[presentation]{beamer}  
> \usepackage{tikz, pgf}  
> \usetikzlibrary{decorations.pathmorphing}  
> \begin{document}  
> \begin{frame}  
> \begin{center}  
> \begin{tikzpicture}  
> \uncover<1-3>{  
> \fill [decorate, decoration={random steps,segment length=2pt,amplitude=2pt}] (0,0) ellipse (0.5cm and 0.4cm);  
> }  
> \end{tikzpicture}  
> \end{center}  
> \end{frame}  
> \end{document} 
> ```
:::

You can set the random seed each time you draw the ellipse, like so:

```latex
\documentclass[presentation]{beamer}
\usepackage{tikz, pgf}
\usetikzlibrary{decorations.pathmorphing}
\begin{document}

\begin{frame}
\begin{center}
\begin{tikzpicture}
\uncover<1-3>{
\pgfmathsetseed{1234} % Choose a four-digit number here
\fill [decorate, decoration={random steps,segment length=2pt,amplitude=2pt}] (0,0) ellipse (0.5cm and 0.4cm);
}
\end{tikzpicture}
\end{center}
\end{frame}

\end{document} 
```

The best part is that `\pgfmathsetseed` is local so outside this tikzpicture environment the pseudo-random number generator will behave as usual.

And by the way [random.org](http://www.random.org/) is a cool place to get random numbers to use as seeds.  [Here's](http://www.random.org/integers/?num=1&min=1000&max=9999&col=5&base=10&format=html&rnd=new) one just for you.
